newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer defector says Cambodian politicians killed.
newsitem.headline: Khmer defector says Cambodian politicians killed.

text.p: Government troops are advancing on a key Khmer Rouge base after receiving reports the rebels had killed 12 government staff missing in their territory for almost two months, a senior officer said on Friday.
Armed forces deputy chief of staff Lieutenant-General Nhiek Bun Chhay told reporters the army had stepped up a gradual push on Anlong Veng, believed held by feared one-legged rebel commander Ta Mok.
He said the nearest government base was about four km (2-1/2 miles) from the rebel stronghold, near the Thai border.
"There are only three left. Two pilots and (military negotiator Colonel) Nin Pin," Nhiek Bun Chhay said of the government employees, citing a report from a guerrilla defector.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the Cambodian People's Party, which formed an uneasy alliance with the royalist FUNCINPEC party after U.N.-run polls in 1993, said last month he had received reports that only three of the 15-strong government team were alive.
The 15, most of them from First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC, flew by helicopter into rebel territory on February 14 to conduct negotiations on defections.
Nhiek Bun Chhay, a FUNCINPEC member, on Friday quoted the defector as saying 12 of the officials were shot dead on the day their helicopter landed.
Another general, asking not to be named, told Reuters the army would ask Thailand to let 300 Cambodian troops cross Thai territory to attack Anlong Veng.
"The result of Anlong Veng will be clear in May," he said.

The Maoist-inspired Khmer Rouge, whose 1975-79 "killing fields" rule left more than a million Cambodians dead, signed a U.N.-sponsored peace pact in 1990, but reneged on the deal and have been fighting the coalition government formed in 1993.
The movement began unravelling in August when Ieng Sary, foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge years in power, split with hardliners, triggering a mass defection.
The rebels, holed up at Anlong Veng, are believed to number fewer than 2,000 following the defections.
